title: Pakistan FBR Wealth Statement under Section 116 of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001
description: The Federal Board of Revenue's (FBR) official 'Manual Return' workbook for individuals, Tax Year 2024 edition, worksheet 'Wealth Statement' — the mandatory net-worth disclosure required under section 116 of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001, filed alongside (not instead of) the individual income tax return already modelled as `pk/fbr/annual-individual-income-tax-return-it-1b`. This document is a companion schema within Pakistan's already-open Taxes vertical, not a new vertical. It is scoped to the statement's category-level reportable figures: the taxpayer's identification block; the 14 numbered non-business asset categories (Sr. 1–14, e.g. Agricultural Property, Investment, Motor Vehicle) that sum to Total Assets inside Pakistan; assets held outside Pakistan; Total Assets; the Credit/Loan liability category and Total Liabilities; the year-over-year net-assets reconciliation (Net Assets Current/Previous Year, Increase/Decrease, Inflows and Outflows each broken into their own distinct, individually labelled sub-items, Personal Expenses, and the Unreconciled Amount); disposed assets during the year; and the verification/declaration block. Out of scope for this version: the leaf-level sub-item breakdown beneath each of the 14 asset categories and the single liability category (e.g. Investment's own thirteen sub-item rows — Account, Annuity, Bond, Certificate, Debenture, Deposit, Fund, Instrument, Insurance Policy, Security, Stock/Share, Unit, Others — each itself carrying up to five columns: Form, Account/Instrument No., Institution Name, Share %, Value at Cost). The source workbook's own `dataValidations` confirm these leaf rows, not the category-total rows, are the cells actually constrained as fillable numeric entries (`greaterThanOrEqual 0`) — mirroring the sibling `annual-individual-income-tax-return-it-1b` document's own Sr. 1 (Property) exclusion, where the same signal (no data-validation on a category-total cell) was the basis for treating a subtotal as out of scope. Modelling all fifteen categories' leaf rows individually, given this spec's repeating-value primitive (GSP-0009) remains Proposed and not yet available, would require flattening dozens of same-shaped rows per category into several hundred individually-named fields for what is fundamentally one repeating (description, value) table structure repeated fifteen times — a disproportionate expansion for a companion schema whose core purpose, the net-worth reconciliation, is fully captured at the category-total level already reportable here. This document describes the form only; it does not submit anything on the filer's behalf, and does not imply endorsement by the Islamic Republic of Pakistan or the Federal Board of Revenue. GovSchema is independent and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or operated by the Government of Pakistan.

verification.notes:
GOV-5731 ('GovSchema Standard Research'). `annual-individual-income-tax-return-it-1b`'s own v1.0.0 description (GOV-3104, 2026-07-15) explicitly flagged this same workbook's Wealth Statement worksheet as 'a strong companion-schema candidate for a future cycle' but left it unauthored. This cycle re-scanned CATALOG.md fresh, found every disclosed 5-of-6-vertical jurisdiction gap already a confirmed dead end or an extensively-rescreened weak/unresolved candidate (AE Passport, BA/JM/MN/TT National ID or Visa, TN DMV all previously exhausted), and picked up this pre-flagged, already-open-vertical companion instead. Independently re-fetched the source this cycle via plain `curl` (no login/CAPTCHA gate): HTTP 200, size 104,097 bytes, sha256 `4e2f9874e9a910713fae9a182fc5c5a578bcfd2649d2031f8144c8b5fba96b9f` — identical to the byte count and hash GOV-3104 recorded for the same workbook, confirming no revision since. Unzipped directly with Python's `zipfile` (no `unzip`/pip/openpyxl in this environment); parsed `xl/worksheets/sheet9.xml` (the 'Wealth Statement' sheet, confirmed via `xl/workbook.xml`'s own `<sheets>` listing and cross-checked against the sheet's own printed title row) cell-by-cell from the raw XML, alongside `xl/sharedStrings.xml` and the sheet's own `dataValidations` block.

**Scope decision.** The sheet's `dataValidations` carry exactly two rules: a `type="whole"` 13-digit-range rule on the CNIC cells (`C3:H3`, `G178:H178`, identical to the sibling IT-1B document's own CNIC constraint), and a `greaterThanOrEqual 0` rule whose `sqref` union (`J8:J17 J20:J29 J32:J35 J38:J41 J48:J51 J54:J76 J79:J85 J88:J95 J102:J104 J107:J110 J113:J116 J118 J121:J124 J146:J153 J156 J159:J167 J176:J177 J134:J137 J127:J130`) covers every leaf sub-item row across all fifteen asset/liability categories but excludes every category-total row (e.g. `J6`, `J18`, `J30`, `J131`, `J138`, `J154`) and every reconciliation subtotal row (`J155`, `J157`, `J158`, `J168`, `J169`, `J173`, `J174`) — confirmed by checking each of those specific cells directly for a `<f>` formula element: none carry one except `J173` (Unreconciled Amount, `=SUM(J158)-SUM(J168)-SUM(J169)`, evaluating to `0` in the template). This is the same 'no direct-entry validation on a subtotal cell' signal the sibling IT-1B document's own v1.0.0 used to exclude Sr. 1 (Property)'s sub-item breakdown — applied here at registry scale, since it recurs across all fifteen categories, not just one. Given GSP-0009 (repeating-value fields) remains Proposed and CEO-gated, this version models the category-total figures (the same level IT-1B itself models its headline income lines at) rather than fabricating a false subtotal-vs-leaf distinction or flattening every leaf row into hundreds of individually-named fields; the full leaf-level breakdown is left as disclosed, open backlog for a future companion/minor-version cycle.

**Disclosed structural findings**, each confirmed directly against the raw XML: (1) the 'Cash (Non-business)' category (Sr. 12, Code 7012) prints a formula label '[Sum of 12 i to 12 x]' implying ten sub-item rows, but the sheet carries exactly one physical row beneath it ('Notes & Coins', row 118, no roman-numeral marker at all) — a mismatch between the printed bracket instruction and the actual row count, distinct from every sibling category where the bracket count and physical row count agree; (2) the 'Inflows' category (Sr. 23, Code 7049) enumerates its own sub-items with roman numerals i, ii, iii, iv, vi, vii, viii, ix, x — 'v' is skipped entirely, a genuine gap in the source's own numbering (nine sub-items printed under a bracket reading '23 (i) to 23(x)', which would imply ten) confirmed by checking every row between the iv and vi entries for a missed cell; (3) row 5's 'Business Address*' carries a printed required-field asterisk with no visible conditional ('only if applicable') qualifier anywhere on the sheet, unlike the form's own conditional patterns seen elsewhere in this registry — modelled as `required: true` per the form's literal marking, disclosed here as a plausible over-broad requiredness a future cycle might revisit if a filer-facing instruction sheet surfaces; (4) Sr. 17's own printed formula label '[15+16]' (Total Assets) and Sr. 20's '[17-19]' (Net Assets Current Year) were both independently confirmed arithmetically consistent with this document's own field set, unlike the sibling IT-1B document's own disclosed Sr. 17 bracket-label defect — no equivalent defect found on this sheet's reconciliation section.

2 valid mock scenarios (a modest salaried individual reporting only a residential property, one bank deposit under Investment, and no liabilities; a self-employed individual reporting agricultural property, business capital, a motor vehicle, a small loan liability, and a full Inflows/Outflows reconciliation with a foreign-remittance inflow and a gift outflow) plus 4 mutation-control fixtures (a missing statically-required field, an invalid `declarantCapacity` enum value, an out-of-range CNIC pattern violation, a negative amount on a `minimum: 0` field) are committed under `conformance/pk/fbr/wealth-statement/1.0.0/`. An ephemeral, from-scratch conformance checker (deriving required/pattern/minimum rules directly from this schema's own `fields[]`, discarded after use, not committed) ran all 6: both valid scenarios at 0 errors, all 4 mutation controls each raising exactly 1 error. Validated clean with `node tools/validate.mjs` and `node tools/validate-ajv.mjs`, individually and as part of the full registry run.
